# Flexbox Froggy: Playgarden adaptation

Source: Thomas Park, `thomaspark/flexboxfroggy@9a6feab850a56cbe9ad90f3afcc95e88335bbec8`.

The complete original game is retained: all 24 authored lessons; full multilingual instructions, including Tim Guo's Simplified Chinese; property-reference help and value insertion; direct course selection; hidden-instruction/random practice modes; per-course drafts and solved markers; color-assistance artwork; original browser Flexbox rendering; and the original uncounted ending with 25 celebrating frogs.

`upstream/` contains precisely the approved 26 source/license files. Readable dependency distributions have moved from upstream's `node_modules/` paths to `third-party/` so they are deliberately tracked, not dependency installations. `source-manifest.json` preserves both path identities, byte lengths, SHA-256 and Git blob SHA-1. The separately fetched CC-BY-3.0 text has the same exact bytes as the approved source package. The original supplemental record is retained verbatim as `supplied-supplement-manifest.json`; there was no blob correction.

`scripts/flexbox-froggy/adapt.py` reproducibly changes the original game controller at explicit string anchors. It removes unsafe generic storage startup, locale inference, old page handlers and its immediate boot. It delegates handlers, checks and previous/next requests to the adapter, keeps the original renderer/menu/docs/translation/CSS-writing/win routines, and retains the real position/color checker. The sole checker hardening counts matching color/position pairs one-to-one, so overlapping duplicate frogs cannot satisfy several pads. No lesson target or successful CSS string is substituted for the browser's layout result.

`public/flexbox-froggy/adapter.js` owns the isolated page lifecycle. Its generation tokens invalidate input debounce, view transitions and two-second advance callbacks whenever input, pause, retry, navigation, visibility, resize or disposal supersedes them. View-transition callbacks verify both generation and editor contents before applying or comparing. Pause cancels delayed advance; resuming rechecks, and the player chooses Next again. Input drafts are saved immediately through the parent, rather than waiting for unreliable iframe unload.

The iframe uses `sandbox="allow-scripts"` without same-origin, popup, form, download or top-navigation capabilities. Its opaque-origin page has no localStorage access and cannot access the host DOM. The bridge verifies source window, parent origin and a per-mount random session. The React host validates all state and level bounds and stores only `playgarden.flexbox-froggy.v1.state`; the existing shell owns `.selected`. Internal navigation requests the bounded host callback before changing any internal index. React development effect replay does not accidentally dispose the live frame. The host also saves the latest accepted snapshot during unmount, and frame destruction removes all remaining execution.

The saved `earnedEnding` milestone is separate from `ending`, which describes only the current screen. It is set only when the real final-course check succeeds and the original Next action reaches the ending, and it requires the final course among the actually solved names. The shell may reopen the first unfinished course after reload; its ordinary snapshots preserve the earned milestone, so selecting the last course again restores the original ending. A current-course retry preserves that history but starts a fresh attempt; clearing all practice records clears it. Older states migrate an earned final screen only when the final course is also recorded as solved. This never grants any unsolved course or fabricates all-24 completion.

User text is parsed into a detached CSSStyleDeclaration only after allowlisting the eight Flexbox properties used by these lessons. CSS.supports validates browser semantics; keyword/integer syntax excludes URLs, functions, variables, selectors, escapes and `!important`. Only the original pond or authored frog subset receives the serialized declarations. Alternative layouts, order integers and `flex-flow` shorthand remain accepted by the original objective check. A restrictive local content policy separately blocks remote scripts/styles/images/fonts, connections, forms and embeds.

The original HTML wrapper was not copied or published because it contains ads and analytics. The replacement retains the course/editor/pond structure with proper buttons, a touch-friendly textarea, accessible property help, pause, current-course retry, language/difficulty/color controls and an in-page reset confirmation. Original broad CSS is isolated in the sandbox; additive CSS supplies system fonts and responsive sizing. Original CSS and all twelve artwork SVGs are unchanged. Original victory text and tableau remain; promotional paragraphs after the victory paragraph are hidden at presentation time. The host says explicitly that completing the last course may show the ending while other courses remain unfinished; only 24 separately solved names yields the all-course completion message.

Property help and the course menu participate in the sidebar's normal document flow, like the settings panel. They therefore enlarge the reported iframe height and remain reachable with ordinary page scrolling on a phone. The original help text and CSS insertion handlers remain intact; the reproducible controller patch removes only help positioning offsets and scopes the current-course number to the indicator. Additive controls provide an explicit help close button and keyboard access. The targeted journey keeps genuine taps on help values, color settings, the course menu and the non-destructive reset-cancel path, with open-panel screenshots for review.

Licenses remain separate: Thomas Park's code/text/CSS MIT; his twelve SVGs CC-BY-3.0 Unported; jQuery/Sizzle and Animate.css MIT; Playgarden adapter contributions GPL-3.0-only. NOTICE.txt includes full terms, attribution and the original README's complete translator credits. No images are relabeled as GPL/MIT, and no endorsement is implied.

No upstream build, dependency installation, game script execution, browser session, unit test, or exhaustive solver was used to prepare this package. Preparation uses static source hashing, XML parsing, anchored text transformations, JavaScript syntax checks and deterministic ZIP creation. The supplied single E2E journey must be run by the integration owner after independent review, on both desktop and touch-size projects; screenshot review is required before publication.

## Reproduce source package

From repository root, using Python's standard library:

1. `python3 scripts/flexbox-froggy/adapt.py`
2. `python3 scripts/flexbox-froggy/package-source.py`
3. `python3 scripts/flexbox-froggy/verify-sources.py`

The browser runtime itself needs no build. The surrounding existing Playgarden React build imports `src/games/FlexboxFroggy.tsx`. `docs/flexbox-froggy-catalog-entry.json`, `docs/flexbox-froggy-runtime-source-addendum.json`, `docs/flexbox-froggy-source-map.json` and `docs/flexbox-froggy-notice-addendum.md` are integration-owner addenda; they do not edit the shared registry automatically.

The final targeted command is `npm run test:e2e -- e2e/flexbox-froggy.spec.ts`. That single file exercises physical text entry, incorrect CSS, original property help including close/reopen, an equivalent valid answer, URL/rule-breakout rejection, first/middle/final real layouts, color assistance, course-menu reset cancellation, cancelled delayed validation and Next, parent-aligned internal navigation, saved draft reentry, the actual ending, reload, 320px overflow and route disposal. There are no injected wins, state setters, solved-progress fixtures or complete-campaign solvers.
